notes: Chosen hook (index 0): '1.54M DAILY DEEPSEEK USERS'. Clear in 2s: 8. Curiosity: 5 (a big number, but no question or tension). Concrete number/name: 9. Promise kept: 5. Stake: 2 (acceptable, since no option is reader-impact). The main problem is scope. On the cover, 'DeepSeek users' reads as users of DeepSeek, the chatbot and app. Slides 1-2 and 6 say the figure is daily active users of the Harness agent platform, self-reported, and that how the count maps to Harness users is not explained. A reader who does not swipe will take it as the DeepSeek chatbot's audience. That would be a small number for DeepSeek, so it invites a wrong comparison. The cover also drops the 'self-reported' flag that the slides keep stressing. The 'daily' wording and the CHINA AI · TOOLS tag do not fix the scope. hook_pick_reason argues the line limit leaves no room for 'agent', but this wording still misleads. Other options (indices are 0-based): 1 '35,000 PLUGINS IN 3 MONTHS' is concrete and backed by slide 4, but it has no name, so it is unclear whose plugins. 2 'DEEPSEEK VS US AGENT TOOLS' overpromises, as the reason says. 3 'DEEPSEEK WANTS AN AGENT OS' has a name, makes the reader ask what an agent OS is, and is backed by slide 5, whose title is 'DeepSeek is aiming at an agent OS', and by the quoted 'operating system of the AI agent era'. It is accurate as a stated plan and has no scope confusion, though it has no number. Use option 3. If the number must stay, rewrite it as '1.54M DAILY / HARNESS USERS' if it fits the 16-character line limit, or '1.54M DAILY / AGENT USERS'. hook_types labels are honest (number, number, rivalry, claim). hook_pick_reason has an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' sentence, since the articles state no effect on ordinary readers. Its pick rationale is the weak part.
